params.name: input_tiltseries
params.label: Input tilt series:
params.help: STAR file with input tilt-series

params.name: create_settings.bin_angpix
params.label: Target pixel size
params.help:
--bin_angpix in create_settings: Choose the binning exponent automatically to match this target pixel size in Angstrom. 
0 = No binning, 1 = Bin 2x, etc.

params.name: create_settings.eer_ngroups
params.label: EER groups
params.help: (--eer_ngroups) EER grouping.

params.name: eerSampling
params.label: EER upsampling factor
params.help:
Render EER movies in super-resolution (EER only, ignored for other formats). Directly determines the maximum achievable resolution.

How it works: Warp decides the rendering size from the size of the gain reference, so the wrapper upsamples the 4k gain by pixel replication into the job folder (e.g. <gain>_eer2x.gain) and runs create_settings with --angpix = input pixel size / factor. A gain that already matches the upsampled size is used as is. A gain reference is required.

'Target pixel size' (binning) is applied after upsampling, e.g. with an input of 4k at 1.19 A/px:
- Upsample 2x, no target -> 8k at 0.595 A/px
- Upsample 2x, target 1.19 -> 8k at 0.595 A/px, binned to 4k at 1.19 A/px
- Upsample 4x, target 0.595 -> 16k at 0.2975 A/px, binned to 8k at 0.595 A/px

The output STAR files contain the final tilt image pixel size (rlnTomoTiltSeriesPixelSize) and point to the upsampled gain, so downstream Warp jobs use the same gain. rlnMicrographOriginalPixelSize keeps the input pixel size.

Downstream tilt series alignment and reconstruction:
- The Warp tilt series settings always use the input (physical) pixel size as --angpix, because Warp reads the image size from the EER header (always 4k). Give --tomo_dimensions in input pixels whatever the upsampling, e.g. 4096x4096x2000 at 1.19 A/px.
- Alignment and reconstruction pixel sizes are absolute, so the binning is relative to the tilt images: 4.76 A/px is bin 8 for 0.595 A/px tilt images and bin 4 for 1.19 A/px ones.

IMPORTANT: Use Warp version 2.0.0dev33 for motion correction with upsampling (set the WARP launcher to warp_launcher_vdev33.sh). Newer development versions (e.g. 2.0.0dev40) have a bug that randomly writes about half of the averages as a 4k image packed into the top quarter of the 8k frame.

params.name: fs_motion_and_ctf.m_range_min
params.label: min
params.help: (--m_range_min) Default: 500. Minimum resolution in Angstrom to consider in fit

params.name: fs_motion_and_ctf.m_range_max
params.label: max
params.help: (--m_range_max) Default: 10. Maximum resolution in Angstrom to consider in fit

params.name: fs_motion_and_ctf.m_bfac
params.label: Bfactor (Aˆ2)
params.help: (--m_bfac)  Default: -500. Downweight higher spatial frequencies using a B-factor, in Angstrom^2

params.name: fs_motion_and_ctf.m_grid
params.label: Grid (XxYxN):
params.help: (--m_grid) Default: 1x1xN. Resolution of the motion model grid in X, Y, and temporal dimensions, separated by 'x': e.g. 5x5x40; empty = auto

params.name: extra_create_settings
params.label: create_settings extra arguments
params.help: Extra arguments to pass to create_settings

params.name: acq.gain
params.label: Gain reference
params.help: Optional gain reference file for motion correction. If set, overrides the value from the emw-import-ts job stored in the input tilt-series STAR file.

params.name: fs_motion_and_ctf.c_range_min
params.label: min
params.help: (--c_range_min) Default: 500. Minimum resolution in Angstrom to consider in fit

params.name: fs_motion_and_ctf.c_range_max
params.label: max
params.help: (--c_range_max) Default: 10. Maximum resolution in Angstrom to consider in fit

params.name: fs_motion_and_ctf.c_defocus_min
params.label: min
params.help: (--c_defocus_min) Default: 500. Minimum resolution in Angstrom to consider in fit

params.name: fs_motion_and_ctf.c_defocus_max
params.label: max
params.help: (--c_defocus_max) Default: 10. Maximum resolution in Angstrom to consider in fit

params.name: fs_motion_and_ctf.c_window
params.label: Window (px)
params.help: (--c_window) Default: 512. Patch size for CTF estimation in binned pixels

params.name: fs_motion_and_ctf.c_grid
params.label: Grid (XxYxN):
params.help: (--c_grid) Resolution of the defocus model grid in X, Y, and temporal dimensions, separated by 'x': e.g. 5x5x40; empty = auto; Z > 1 is purely experimental

params.name: fs_motion_and_ctf.c_use_sum
params.label: Use sum
params.help: (--c_use_sum) Use the movie average spectrum instead of the average of individual frames spectra. Can help in the absence of an energy filter, or when signal is low.

params.name: fs_motion_and_ctf.out_average_halves
params.label: Output averages halves
params.help: (--out_average_halves) Export aligned averages of odd and even frames separately, e.g. for denoiser training

params.name: gpus
params.label: GPUs
params.help: If it is a single number (N), it will represent the total number of GPUs (0..N-1). It there are multiple values, it will be the specific GPUs ID.

params.name: fs_motion_and_ctf.perdevice
params.label: Processes per device
params.help: (--perdevice in fs_motion_and_ctf)

params.label: Launchers
params.help: Launchers to use for the different programs

params.name: register_output_only
params.label: Register output only
params.help: Register output only, without running the job. Output files (e.g. STAR files) will be re-generated, but the the underlying programs will not be executed.

form.help:
Warp wrapper to run the motion correction and CTF estimation. It will run the following programs:

[[https://warpem.github.io/warp/reference/warptools/api/frame_series/?h=fs_motion_and_ctf][fs_motion_and_ctf]]
